title: Identify a usable Spanish verb lemma-frequency dataset and redistribution terms
description:

Compare a small number of credible sources; do not exhaustively collect verbs or generate production data. Resolve pronominal joins and whether frequency covers the base verb or distinct pronominal entry. Distinguish verified usable data from permission-dependent candidates and surface a concrete next decision. CORPES downloadable schema/permissions and AnCora conflicting license descriptions were previously unresolved; other openly licensed annotated Spanish corpora may offer a practical alternative. Capture current primary-source evidence and any small inspection in an isolated research/frequency-source branch/worktree; do not modify the production app, commit, push, or sync. Link the findings in a resolution comment and close only if the investigation is answered. Consult research skill and repo AGENTS.md; claim before work.

title: Define shared user-language fallbacks and target-language build boundaries
description:
## Question

With the user decision that one shared user-language setting controls both UI strings and translation glosses (English initially), what fallback and availability behavior should the spec require, and what varies in each future target-language build? Clarify target language, shared user language, subject labels, grammatical labels, and language-specific inventories without assuming Spanish structures generalize. Decide how to handle a user language whose UI strings exist but glosses are incomplete. Implementing additional languages and iPhone is deferred; preserve a clear route to them.
close_reason: User confirmed complete-only user-language availability, label languages, separate target-language builds, device-language matching, remembered overrides, and whole-app English fallback. Consolidated resolution recorded.

comments.author: Cormac Bracken
comments.text: Confirmed live choices, 18 November 2026: a user language is selectable only when its interface, glosses, and explanatory text are complete for that target-language build. Grammatical headings use the user language; subject pronouns remain in the target language; clarifications use the user language. Future target languages use separate builds with their own grammatical categories, subject/address systems, regional choices, presets, and frequency-ordered verb inventories; current build remains Spanish-only. Initial user-language selection uses a complete bundled match to the device language, otherwise English, and remembers explicit Settings choices. Initial English-only release needs no language selector. Recorded resolved terminology in CONTEXT.md. Device-language matching/lifecycle and unavailable saved-language handling still need live choices; ticket remains in progress.

comments.author: Cormac Bracken
comments.text:
## Resolution — 18 November 2026

Confirmed through the live user discussion, including explicit acceptance of the final device-language and fallback choices and instruction to record and close. This is the consolidated localization and target-language-build decision.

### Shared user language and completeness

One shared user-language preference controls interface strings, grammatical headings, grammatical glosses (including alternatives), and explanatory/clarifying text. English is the initial and fallback user language. There are no separate interface-language and gloss-language preferences.

A user language is available only when all of that content is complete for the particular target-language build and its included verb/form inventory. Complete UI strings with incomplete glosses do not qualify. Completeness covers all supported selectable categories and regional profiles, not just the default preset or currently displayed verb. All required content is bundled for offline operation; no runtime translation or download is required.

A missing translation in a supposedly complete language is a release defect to catch before shipping. It must not become a routine per-string English fallback, a missing grammatical form, or an invitation to show a partly translated language. Genuine grammatical absence remains distinct from missing data under the coverage and interaction decisions. The initial English-only release does not need a language selector; future builds with multiple available user languages expose the shared preference in Settings.

### Labels and target-language content

Grammatical headings use the user language, for example English “Present indicative.” Subject pronouns stay in the target language, for example yo, tú, and usted. Learner-facing clarifications, such as formality, use the user language. Infinitives and conjugated forms remain target-language content; a user-language change does not change the target language, verb identity, or grammatical inventory. Existing subject/form/gloss associations and alternatives remain intact.

### Device language, explicit choices, and fallback

The default is Use device language, resolved at each launch until overridden. Match the device locale against the build's available bundled user languages: exact supported locale first, then its generic language, otherwise English. For example, French Canadian may use a complete generic French translation, but must not silently select a different regional French variant. Unsupported device languages use English for the whole interface and glosses.

In future multilingual Settings, allow an explicit available user-language choice and a Use device language option. Persist the learner's choice locally across launches. An explicit language takes precedence over later device-language changes; Use device language continues to follow them at launch. Concrete preference representation and locale handling contracts belong to Choose clear module contracts and linguistic-data boundaries.

If a saved explicit user language becomes unavailable after an update, switch the whole interface and glosses to English and show a brief explanation. Do not silently mix languages or substitute device-language matching for this case. The fallback operates within the same offline bundled-content policy.

### Separate target-language builds

Keep the initial app a Spanish-only build. Future target languages are separate builds, each defining its own verb inventory and frequency ordering, grammatical categories, subject/address systems, regional choices where applicable, and learner presets. Availability of a user language is assessed separately for each build.

Do not encode Spanish's tense list, six-person assumptions, address systems, or regional choices as requirements that every future target language must satisfy. Preserve clear boundaries between UI, application behavior, linguistic data, and localized strings. Concrete contracts belong to Choose clear module contracts and linguistic-data boundaries; this decision does not require a speculative universal grammar framework.

### Handoff and scope

Resolved terminology is captured in [Domain glossary](/home/cormac/Projects/verb-reference/app/CONTEXT.md). The full policy lives in this ticket; the map indexes it rather than duplicating it. Existing coverage, verification, and interaction decisions remain authoritative in their respective areas.

No newly sharp decision requires another ticket: module contracts, preference/corpus/localization formats, and completeness validation seams fit Choose clear module contracts and linguistic-data boundaries; measurable acceptance checks fit Set specification acceptance, testing, and store-readiness boundaries. Implementation of additional languages, production app/corpus generation, and the iPhone port remain deferred. No production implementation, commit, push, or remote sync was performed.

comments.author: Cormac Bracken
comments.text:
## Resolution — 18 November 2026

Confirmed through the live prototype review and the user's final explicit instruction to close this decision. This is the consolidated interaction decision; earlier comments retain discussion history.

### Search, selection, and scrolling

Keep search at the top, pinned while the page scrolls. Results appear below it in the shared frequency order settled in Define Spanish verb coverage, frequency ordering, regional profiles, and learner presets. An empty query displays the frequency-ordered list for browsing. Search is case-insensitive, accent-insensitive substring matching and explicitly folds n/ñ together: searching n can find ñ. Preserve original spellings in displayed entries and data identities; folding is only for matching.

Tapping a result expands it inline sufficiently to contain every selected table. At most one entry is open; opening another closes the previous entry. Use one continuous page scroll, with the opened entry's header visible below pinned search. Keep the current entry open during search edits if it still matches, otherwise close it. An empty query still matches an open entry. No matches has a clear explanatory message and a way to clear/edit search; do not invent or fetch entries.

### Forms, subject ambiguity, and glosses

The agreed design combines presentation B's tinted cards and left border with presentation C's grouping by identical displayed Spanish forms. Keep the applicable subject/address labels together above the shared form, preserving which grammatical uses the form represents. Accepted alternatives remain together under the coverage policy; missing source data must never masquerade as grammatical absence.

Below a shared form, show concise English grammatical-gloss lines without repeating the Spanish subject-label prefixes. Separate alternative phrases with a middot (·), not a pipe. For example, hablan has these lines:

- they speak · they are speaking
- you (plural) speak · you (plural) are speaking

Retain distinct grammatical meanings even when the surface form is shared; redundant identical gloss text need not be repeated. Use a dash (-) for a genuinely unavailable form and keep the English explanation below it. This supersedes the earlier coverage decision's literal display text “not used”; the underlying grammatical-absence distinction is unchanged. Keep that explanation visible even when ordinary glosses are hidden.

Give each tense a distinct tint and matching left border. Aim for red hues for past-ish tenses and blue hues for future-ish tenses. Tense headings remain explicit so colour is never the sole cue. The prototype's exact colour values are illustrative.

### Settings and defaults

Place the settings icon at the top right of the overall screen, accessible even with no expanded entry. Display the active regional profile below the search box. Put the global Show English glosses switch inside settings.

The settings popover contains regional profile, gloss visibility, Common learner / All modern / Custom tense selection, and individual form-category checkboxes. Regional subject systems, default European profile, exact preset coverage, rare labels, nonfinite coverage, alternatives, and exclusions remain as settled in Define Spanish verb coverage, frequency ordering, regional profiles, and learner presets. The Latin American label must disclose the supported Rioplatense pattern rather than suggest every Latin American variety.

Settings apply globally to all verbs and immediately. Done, Android Back, or tapping outside closes the popover without undoing changes. First-install defaults: European profile, Common learner preset, English glosses shown. Persist regional profile, selected categories/preset, and gloss visibility locally across launches. Search and expanded entry reset between launches. No accounts, collection of user data, or runtime network dependency.

Allow all categories to be unchecked. Show an explanatory No verb forms selected state with a route back to settings, rather than silently selecting a category.

### Accessibility and implementation handoff

Require labelled controls, readable text scaling, keyboard and screen-reader access, descriptive expanded/collapsed state, usable touch targets, and explicit tense labels independent of colour. Preserve subject/form/gloss associations when grouping. The prototype uses 48px control targets and focus outlines; production Android accessibility and large-text verification remain acceptance work.

Primary review asset: [Verb-reference interaction prototype](/home/cormac/Projects/verb-reference/app/prototypes/verb-reference.html). Open directly without dependencies or a server; use presentation D (Combined design), with A/B/C retained as exploration context. Four unverified regular-verb fixtures illustrate the interaction; advanced categories without fixtures are explicitly marked. Prototype state is memory-only. Production persistence, full corpus, and native Android Back behavior are specification requirements, not verified prototype features.

Validation: extracted JavaScript passes node --check; the artifact has no external resources/network dependencies. Automated browser rendering and interaction checks were unavailable because the installed Firefox snap fails with a snap-confine capability error. The user reviewed the prototype and confirmed the design; do not represent that as native-device or assistive-technology validation.

No production app, full corpus, git commit, push, or remote sync was performed. Retain this uncommitted prototype asset; the repository's conservative policy and map notes do not authorize committing a throwaway branch. Remaining localization, module/data contracts (including grouping, search folding, and local preference schema), and measurable acceptance questions belong to the existing decision tickets. No additional decision ticket is needed from this resolution.

title: Define independent two-model verification and disagreement handling
description:
## Question

How will AI-generated conjugations and English grammatical glosses be checked independently by two different LLM models before bundling? Decide whether the generator is separate from both checkers, what independence means (blind inputs, model identity, prompts), record provenance, set agreement and completeness criteria, and decide what happens on disagreement or uncertainty. Distinguish structural validation from linguistic correctness and model agreement from proof. Identify who can approve exceptions and how corrected data is regenerated reproducibly. The user chose two-model checking; external-reference checks are not an assumed requirement.
close_reason: User confirmed the consolidated two-model verification policy, pinned checker identities and effort, lean provenance, targeted rechecks, reduced-coverage approval, and standing maintainer exceptions.

comments.author: Cormac Bracken
comments.text: Confirmed first-round choices, 18 November 2026: Two fresh isolated verification runs by different checking models; the generator may share a model identity with one checker, but generation never counts as verification. Both checking models review every entry and cell, including conjugations, English grammatical glosses, alternatives, and not-used claims. Structural validation is separate from linguistic review; model agreement is a release criterion, not proof. Disagreement or uncertainty blocks the affected entry pending correction and fresh checks; only the maintainer may approve a documented exception, with limits still to be decided. Review isolation, model identity, agreement criteria, provenance, correction/regeneration and exception limits remain open. User also requested selectable-option questions outside Plan mode for wayfinder/grilling/grill-with-docs/grill-me; instruction added to AGENTS.md and mirrored in CLAUDE.md.

comments.author: Cormac Bracken

comments.author: Cormac Bracken
comments.text:
## Proposed consolidated resolution — awaiting final accuracy check, 18 November 2026

### Generation and independent checking
Generation is a separate step; its model may also be one of the checking models, but generation never counts as verification. Checkers are:
- OpenAI GPT-6.1 Sol, exact ID gpt-6.1-sol, medium reasoning effort.
- DeepSeek via Umans, exact pinned ID umans-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017, high reasoning effort.
Use these two different model families/providers. Model substitution or upgrades require an explicit recorded decision, not automatic fallback. Provider routing and remaining request settings are recorded when tooling is built. Documentation establishes IDs/settings, not account access or accuracy on this corpus; no paid calls or corpus generation performed.

Each checker uses a fresh isolated review context containing the candidate content and the same versioned coverage requirements, excluding generator identity/reasoning, the other checker output, and earlier review histories. Shared review requirements/prompts may have provider-specific formatting, recorded in run metadata; prompt differences alone never establish model independence. No mandatory external-reference verification is introduced.

### Completeness and acceptance
Both checkers review every entry and required cell across the full selectable coverage settled in the coverage decision, not just the default preset: regional profiles, simple/compound tenses, commands, nonfinite forms, rare categories, alternatives, defective/impersonal restrictions, and English grammatical glosses. Candidate eligibility is also reviewed; CORPES annotation is not linguistic proof.
Structural validation independently checks inventory/required-cell coverage, identities, duplicates, schema, and machine-checkable invariants. Linguistic review assesses correct and complete Spanish forms, grammar/gloss meaning, alternatives, and justified not-used claims. Missing data is not grammatical absence.
Normal acceptance requires explicit approval by both models of each cell's forms, completeness, and grammatical gloss meaning. Identical English wording is unnecessary. A missing alternative, unsupported form, uncertainty, omitted verdict, malformed/truncated review, or incorrect not-used claim does not pass. Coverage checks must detect absent cells/entries, including material omitted from the candidate itself. Agreement is a release criterion, not proof.

### Disagreement and correction
Disagreement, uncertainty, structural failures, or incomplete reviews block affected content unless covered by a maintainer exception. Preserve failures; do not use majority vote or retry an unchanged linguistic failure until it passes. Transport retries do not convert missing reviews into approval.
Corrections trigger structural validation and two fresh blind checks of changed cells plus cells affected by a known shared mistake. Preserve approvals elsewhere. A corrected surface form or shared gloss affects every cell using it; a known defective review rule invalidates affected approvals even if content is unchanged.
Withhold unresolved entries. Release reduced coverage only with explicit maintainer approval, recording omissions against the intended inventory.

### Lean provenance and reproducibility
Store shared model/provider identities, prompts/coverage versions, settings and tooling versions once per run. Store per-cell content fingerprints and each checker verdict linked to the run, plus failure and exception reasons. Retain accepted versioned data and deterministic packaging inputs. Fingerprints bind the reviewed content and grammatical context, including alternatives and not-used state; review requirements versions identify what was checked.
Full raw generation/review requests and responses are not required. Capture generator identity/settings in shared run metadata, without forcing an exact generator choice in this policy.
Rebuild a bundle deterministically from accepted saved artifacts; fresh LLM calls need not reproduce identical output. Regeneration/correction creates new content fingerprints and runs, invalidating affected approvals under the chosen cell-level rule.

### Maintainer exceptions
Only Cormac as maintainer may approve an exception for ANY failed or missing check, with a documented rationale; no category of check is exempt from this authority. Preserve underlying failures and distinguish exception-based acceptance from two-model approval.
Standing exceptions may apply across future content versions, without automatic expiry on content changes. Record the approving maintainer, rationale, covered entries/cells or dataset/check class, and prospective scope. Apply a standing exception to future versions within that scope until revised or revoked; unrelated failures require their own applicable exception. One-off exceptions remain possible. Exact release mechanics belong in downstream tooling/contracts.

### Evidence and handoff
Official references checked 18 November 2026:
- https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-6.1-sol (ID, medium effort and supported reasoning settings)
- https://app.umans.ai/offers/code/docs and https://app.umans.ai/models/umans-deepseek-v4.1-flash (moving alias versus pinned 1017 ID, high effort)
This is a planning decision, not implementation of the production app or generation tooling. Downstream module/contracts and acceptance/spec tickets consume it.

title: Define Spanish verb coverage, frequency ordering, regional profiles, and learner presets
description:
## Question

Given the inventory research and the user's clarification, what source and inclusion rules provide a fairly comprehensive Spanish verb list with useful frequency ordering? Frequency availability is more important than exhaustively discovering every possible verb; no proof of absolute lexical completeness is required. Decide regional, rare, pronominal, defective, and alternative entries; corpus choice and redistribution suitability; lemma versus inflected-form counts; ties; and entries without measured frequency.

Separately define complete modern conjugation coverage, common learner tense defaults, available presets and individual tense selection, and treatment of alternative, missing, and ambiguous forms. Do not assume a fixed six-row paradigm or that every conjugation has a unique English gloss.

Spanish settings must also offer European / Latin American Spanish alongside tense selection, affecting address/formality and plural forms. Decide the subject systems represented by these profiles, default profile, treatment of tú/vos/usted and vosotros/ustedes, and the boundary between regional display filtering and grammatical coverage. Do not assume all Latin American varieties share one paradigm.

comments.author: Cormac Bracken
comments.text:
## Resolution — 18 November 2026

Resolved through the live user discussion, including the final explicit acceptance of CORPES's own separately listed pronominal lemma counts with the annotation limitation documented. This comment is the consolidated coverage decision; earlier discussion comments provide its history.

### Verb inventory and frequency

Use the user-downloaded CORPES lexical frequency dictionary snapshot dated 18 November 2026. Pin the original artifact by SHA-256 `16203075050080abd4e5eabe35db5723bc74563707ea62244e48d94ba17d38cb` and source URL, not the current general CORPES corpus version. This dictionary reflects the documented press subset across 21 countries. Technical evidence, source attribution/license notice, parser, and limitations live in [Inspect CORPES frequency data for the Spanish verb inventory](/home/cormac/Projects/verb-reference/corpes-inspection-research/research/corpes-inspection.md). Retain that isolated worktree and its uncommitted input/report/script until deliberately incorporated.

Aim for a fairly comprehensive list, prioritizing available frequency data rather than exhaustive discovery. Every included entry must have its own positive measured source lemma count. Select native lemma rows with exact class V and empty form column; never add inflected-detail counts to their lemma total. Include auxiliary-capable verb lemmas. Keep rare and regional verb candidates and count-one entries; impose no arbitrary top-N or frequency floor.

The verified source has 10,399 unique positive V records. The documented conservative single-infinitive screen yields 10,291 candidates, including 285 native pronominal spellings. Quarantine the four grouped alternative labels and 104 non-infinitive labels without splitting, copying, or reallocating their counts. These are candidates for downstream linguistic/content validation, not an already approved production lexicon or a promise that all source annotations are correct. Preserve source identities and provenance; do not silently normalize an entry into a different measured lemma.

Order both regional profiles by the same descending absolute verb-lemma count, with alphabetical ties. Counts aggregate the source-assigned inflected uses, not merely the infinitive spelling. Do not reuse the published all-POS rank as a verb-only rank or imply a frequency difference between tied entries. Use a documented deterministic alphabetical comparison. The regional setting changes forms, not ordering.

A native separately listed pronominal lemma's own CORPES count satisfies the separate-frequency rule. Document that corpus annotation may be imperfect and does not prove semantic purity of every token. Do not copy a base count to an absent pronominal entry, use a surface-infinitive count as an all-inflection count, or infer counts from grouped labels. Thus arrepentirse is eligible with its own count of 1,451; irse is excluded because it has no native entry. Exclude unranked entries. No contextual pronominal-only recount is required by this decision.

The user explicitly deferred the permission issue; it is not an outstanding blocker to this planning decision. The downloaded file itself declares CC BY-SA 4.0, correcting the earlier uncertainty about its header; retain that provenance notice. No external permission request, publication, or distribution has been performed or authorized here.

### Regional profiles

Offer European and Latin American Spanish in user settings alongside tense selection. European is the default. These are the specified supported patterns, not a claim to implement every regional variety.

- European: informal singular tú, formal singular usted, informal plural vosotros/vosotras, formal plural ustedes.
- Latin American: informal singular vos, formal singular usted, ustedes for both informal and formal plural address. Use the chosen Rioplatense pattern: hablás/comés/vivís; affirmative commands hablá/comé/viví; present subjunctive hables/comas/vivas. Do not silently substitute tú.

Both profiles retain the other applicable subjects. Address/formality is distinct from morphological agreement: usted and ustedes use third-person verb agreement. Do not assume a universal six-row display or require a unique surface form/gloss for every subject. Row grouping and preference persistence belong to the interaction decision.

### Tense selection and coverage

Support individual checkboxes and Common learner, All modern, and Custom selections. Common learner is the default: present indicative, preterite indicative, imperfect indicative, affirmative and negative commands, and simple infinitive, gerund, and participle.

All modern includes all supported ordinary modern simple and haber-based compound tense categories, affirmative/negative commands, and simple/compound nonfinite forms. Specifically, its finite tenses are:

- Indicative: present, preterite, imperfect, future, conditional, present perfect, pluperfect, future perfect, conditional perfect.
- Subjunctive: present, imperfect, present perfect, pluperfect.

Keep pretérito anterior and simple/compound future subjunctive available through individual selection, labelled rare and excluded from All modern. These three categories complete the broader selectable finite inventory. Include accepted -ra/-se alternatives where applicable; alternatives are realizations of a category, not extra tense categories.

Keep constructions such as estar + gerund and ir a + infinitive outside the conjugation tables. Their exclusion does not remove the ordinary haber-based compound tenses or compound infinitive/gerund.

### Alternatives, absence, glosses, and handoff

Show accepted alternatives together. Mark genuinely unavailable forms “not used”; missing data is a release defect, not grammatical absence. Respect defective and impersonal uses rather than inventing ordinary cells. English grammatical glosses can have alternatives and ambiguity; no one-to-one surface-form/gloss requirement is introduced.

This resolves coverage and selection policy only. No production app or full production corpus was generated. Independent two-model verification and disagreement handling, interaction details/persistence, language fallbacks, module contracts, and acceptance criteria remain in their existing decision tickets. The source and domain results make no additional sharp ticket necessary: those existing tickets already cover the remaining route. The inspected corpus evidence must inform verification and data boundaries without turning corpus annotation into a claim of linguistic truth.
